historical_growth.fcf_series_basis: Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC - interest income: FY2020 1,789; FY2022 818; FY2025 1,810.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (2.3%) diverges >30% from EPS 5yr CAGR (16.9%). The EPS CAGR starts at the FY2020 hog-cycle low (5.6c), and equity is depressed by the 2021 US$1.93bn buyback and the FY2025 US$1.8bn of ordinary-plus-special dividends. Neither is a forward growth rate; the revenue 5yr CAGR (1.8%) and the 7yr CAGR (3.1%) bracket the base path.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF 3yr CAGR (30%) is endpoint noise: FY2022 owner FCF was depressed by a working-capital build. The 5yr owner-FCF CAGR (0.2%) vs reported FCF 5yr (1.2%) gap is interest income, not SBC; SBC is not growing faster than cash flow (it only appeared in FY2025 with the Smithfield IPO).

scenario_narratives.base: Packaged meats (82% of FY2025 operating profit) keeps compounding low-single-digit in the US and Europe while China packaged volumes stabilise rather than recover; the pork segment runs a normal hog cycle around the current oversupply in China and the EU, so group EBITDA fades from ~11.5% to an 11% mid-cycle margin. Smithfield's Sioux Falls replacement lifts capex to ~3.5% of revenue in 2027-29 without margin credit. Revenue grows ~3% (Smithfield's low-single-digit guide, poultry and Morliny organic growth), and the 13% Smithfield and 30% Shuanghui minorities take ~18.5% of after-tax profit.
scenario_narratives.bull: The China and EU hog cycles turn up together from the 2026 lows (China hog prices -27.5% y/y, EU carcass -20% in H1 2026) while US hog production stays profitable on cheap feed; China packaged meats returns to volume growth through the new-channel/product transformation; Morliny's Wolf/Argal platform and Smithfield's Nathan's brand lift packaged mix; Sioux Falls delivers the promised efficiency. EBITDA margin steps up to ~12.3% and revenue grows 4-5% early.
scenario_narratives.bear: A repeat of the FY2023 trough: China and EU pork stay in loss as ASF (Spain, Germany) and the Chinese supply glut persist, US processing spreads narrow and the 47% China tariff keeps US pork exports shut; China packaged volumes keep shrinking (-3.8% in FY2025). Margin drops to ~9.3% in 2027 and only recovers to a 10% mid-cycle, revenue shrinks in 2027 with hog prices, and the Sioux Falls spend runs over budget.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value WH Group as a mid-cycle integrated protein processor whose packaged-meats franchise now carries the earnings, on attributable owner FCF after the Shuanghui and Smithfield minorities. Do not capitalise the FY2024-25 peak-ish US hog margins or the FY2023 trough; cap the exit at 12x FCF because the pork segment is a commodity cycle.
key_risks_to_valuation: Hog-cycle and biological fair-value volatility in the pork segment (China pork in loss, EU pork profit down 98% in H1 2026)
African swine fever (Spain, Germany) and foot-and-mouth disease shutting export markets
China packaged-meats volume decline and channel shift
US-China tariffs on US pork (~47%) and further trade escalation
Further sell-downs of Smithfield raise the NCI leakage (offset by cash proceeds, typically paid out as special dividends)
HKD/China listing discount: the stock has traded at ~6-8x earnings for years; the 12x FCF exit is above the stock's own historical multiple range

inputs.share_count_basis: 12,830.22m weighted average basic = diluted shares, H1 2026 interim note 7 (diluted EPS 5.99c vs basic 6.00c, so dilution is immaterial). Held FLAT: no non-SBC issuance; the parent has not repurchased since the 2021 US$1,931m buyback (14,733m -> 12,830m).
inputs.net_debt_note: 30 June 2026 interim: borrowings 2,841 current + 1,573 non-current = 4,414 (senior notes 1,988, bank 2,421, third-party 5). Cash 3,762 = cash and bank balances 2,201 + Treasury Products 1,561 (time deposits >3m 1,310, FVTPL 163, debt investments at amortised cost 88). Pledged/restricted deposits (109) excluded. Lease liabilities (99 + 396 = 495) EXCLUDED because leases are charged in the flows (treatment B). Treasury Products are in the bridge, so their interest income is stripped from EBITDA (matching-asset rule).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 AR cash-flow statement line 3774 'Equity-settled share-based payment of a subsidiary' US$24m (Smithfield post-IPO awards); nil at parent FY2020-FY2024; H1 2026 US$12m. No net-share-settlement taxes disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes 0).

inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T08:08:05Z regular HKEX close (Friday; 2026-10-11 is a Sunday)
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD build, because the reporting and debt currency is USD and the largest segment (North America, ~53% of operating profit) is USD. Rf 4.3% (10y UST), ERP 5.5%, beta 0.85 for a protein processor with ~36% of profit from China -> CoE ~9.0%; pre-tax cost of debt ~5% (BBB+/Baa2), ~10% debt weight -> WACC ~8.5%. Same WACC in every scenario: hog-cycle, ASF and China-demand risk live in the scenario flows and weights, not in a premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: lease cash (FY2025 principal 85 in financing + lease interest 21 = 106, 0.38% of revenue) deducted via lease_cost_pct_path; D&A path EXCLUDES right-of-use depreciation (FY2025 PP&E 620 + intangibles 15 = 635, 2.27% of revenue); lease liabilities excluded from net debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows made attributable-only via a combined tax/leakage driver: cash tax 21% then NCI share 18.5% of after-tax profit -> cash_tax_rate_path 35.6% = 1 - 0.79 x 0.815. NCI share: H1 2026 NCI profit 174 / total 944 = 18.4% (Shuanghui Development 29.67% minority ~US$219m/yr + Smithfield 12.99% minority after the Jan-2025 IPO and Sep-2025 secondary, which only contributed US$100m for a part year in FY2025). NO NCI deduction in the bridge (would double-charge). Calibration: FY2025 modelled attributable NOPAT 1,630 vs reported attributable profit before bio-FV 1,591 + after-tax attributable finance cost ex leases (~80) - attributable interest income (~52) = 1,619; ties within 1%. Cross-check: implied NCI value ~US$3.9bn vs market value of the minorities ~US$4.6bn (Shuanghui 000895.SZ RMB23.79 x ~3,465m sh / 6.683 x 29.67% = ~3.7bn; SFD US$18.61 x ~393m x 13% = ~0.95bn). Simplification: the leakage is applied to EBIT, not to (D&A - capex); with capex above D&A during the Sioux Falls build this is slightly conservative.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (component route) with the non-US/cyclical adaptations, routed via .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md 'Operating company, non-US or cyclical'. WH Group is an operating company (pork and packaged meats, US/China/Europe), not a holdco: it consolidates Smithfield (87%) and Shuanghui Development (70.33%) and its value is their free cash flow. No prior DCF and no memory entry, so this is a fresh build. EBITDA base is BEFORE biological fair-value adjustments (FY2025 3,377, H1 2026 1,681), and ex interest income (FY2025 81) because the Treasury Products are in the bridge -> FY2025 underlying 3,296 = 11.76% of revenue. Margin path is MID-CYCLE: FY2018-FY2025 EBITDA margin averaged ~10% across two hog cycles (trough FY2023 7.6%, FY2020 8.2%), but FY2024-FY2025 and H1 2026 have held ~12% even with China pork in loss and EU pork profit down 98%, because packaged meats (82% of FY2025 operating profit) now dominates; base fades from 11.5% to 11.0%. SBC-zero at parent; Smithfield's subsidiary SBC (~0.09% of revenue) kept explicit, so house and street nearly coincide. Buybacks: none since 2021; the flat count is the record, not funded by repurchases. Capex carries the US$1.3bn Sioux Falls replacement plant (construction H1 2027 to end-2028). Bolt-on M&A (Nathan's ~US$450m, Argal, Wolf) is NOT modelled as capex; growth from M&A is likewise excluded from the organic revenue path. Discounting is from FY2025 year-end per house convention against a 30 June 2026 balance sheet; H1 dividends (US$840m) are already out of that cash. Dividend policy: FY2025 HK$0.61/share ordinary (~9% yield at the current price) plus special dividends from the Smithfield sell-downs.
inputs.dividend_note: Dividends are declared in HKD (DividendPerShareHKD kpi); FY2025 HK$0.20 interim + HK$0.41 final.

base.growth_rates_rationale: H1 2026 revenue +3.3%; Smithfield guides low-single-digit growth ex Nathan's; FY2018-25 revenue CAGR 3.1% nominal USD. Organic only.
base.ebitda_margin_rationale: FY2026 from H1 2026 12.2% before bio-FV less ~0.3pp interest income and a softer H2 China/EU hog market; fades to 11.0% mid-cycle (above the ~10% FY2018-25 average because packaged-meats mix has risen and Smithfield exited much of its company-owned hog production).
base.capex_rationale: FY2026 ~US$600m (H1 265). FY2027-29 adds the US$1.3bn Sioux Falls plant (~US$430m/yr) on ~2.3% maintenance. Thereafter 2.7%, just above D&A to fund 2.5% growth.
base.cash_tax_rate_rationale: Combined driver: 21% cash tax (FY2021-25 cash tax paid / PBT = 20.4%; book ETR 23.6%) then 18.5% NCI leakage. See inputs.nci_treatment.
base.wc_capture_rationale: Manufacturer: inventories 3,097 + biological assets 1,038 + receivables 1,489 less trade payables 1,121 and accruals 1,802 = ~US$2.7bn, ~10% of revenue; growth consumes cash.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25% (above the 15% default): the business has hit a trough margin twice in six years (FY2020, FY2023), ASF is live in two EU markets, ~36% of profit is in China with a contracting packaged-meats market, and US-China pork tariffs are a single-regulator risk. Base 50%: H1 2026 shows the packaged-meats franchise held group margin through a two-region pork downturn. Bull 25% (below the 35% default): it needs the China and EU hog cycles to turn together AND China packaged volumes to recover, two independent things.
probability_weighted.band_note: House/street band is degenerate: SBC is ~0.09% of revenue (Smithfield subsidiary awards only), so house and street differ by ~2.5% and the printed band_position (about -1,600%) carries no information; read it as n/a.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
